content: Theria is a subclass of mammals that give birth to live young without the use of a shelled egg. This group includes both eutherians (placental mammals) and metatherians (marsupials and their ancestors). Humans are included within this subclass. Therians possess external ears, and most species are capable of suckling on a nipple. Additionally, they have an ankle structure that is specialized for enhanced power and a wide range of motion. Therians are often categorized based on their specialized dentition. Nearly all currently living (extant) mammals belong to the therian subclass. The only exceptions to this are the platypus and echidnas (spiny anteaters), which are prototherian monotremes.
